exhibits.title: Spot Price
exhibits.statement: Solana (SOL) traded at $89.1100 as of 2026-11-08 09:11:53 UTC, -0.08% over one hour and -1.15% over twenty-four hours.

exhibits.title: 24-Hour Trading Range
exhibits.statement: Over twenty-four hours the price ranged from $88.7100 to $90.0600; spot sits at 30% of that range.

exhibits.title: Seven-Day Trend
exhibits.statement: Price is -6.61% over seven days. The 24-hour average ($89.4255) is below the 72-hour average ($90.2577). Spot is 7.93% below the seven-day high of $96.7814 and 0.45% above the seven-day low of $88.7100.

exhibits.title: Volatility & Momentum
exhibits.statement: Realized volatility computed from hourly closes is 2.85% per day. The 14-hour relative strength index reads 40.6, conventionally neutral.

exhibits.title: Liquidity
exhibits.statement: Twenty-four-hour trading volume was $848.45 million, equal to 1.61% of the $52.67 billion market capitalization.

exhibits.title: Market Sentiment
exhibits.statement: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index reads 28 ("Fear"), versus 34 7 days earlier.

exhibits.title: Chainlink Price Feed
exhibits.statement: The Chainlink SOL/USD Data Feed on Ethereum mainnet last reported $89.9725, 18.5 hours before the spot quote and +0.97% against the spot price in Exhibit A. Practice positions are entered and settled at this mark.

arguments.text:
May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price of SOL is anchored near the lower bound of its 24‑hour range, sitting at just 30% of that range, indicating limited upside potential within the day’s swing and a high probability of price compression toward the median [Ex. B, A].  

2. Realized volatility is modest at 2.85% per day and the RSI of 40.6 signals a neutral but slightly bearish momentum, reinforcing the view that any bullish thrust would be muted and likely reversed before the 24‑hour settlement [Ex. D].  

3. Market sentiment is firmly in fear, with the Fear & Greed Index at 28, and the Chainlink feed—a binding reference for practice positions—prices SOL 0.97% above the spot, further reducing any upside bias for a long entry [Ex. F, G].  

The Bull rests.

May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price is entrenched near the bottom of its 24‑hour range, sitting at only 30% of that band (Ex. B), indicating that any modest upward pressure will encounter limited resistance and should pull price toward the range midpoint.  

2. Momentum is neutral (RSI 40.6, Ex. D) while seven‑day averages remain above the current level (72‑hour average $90.2577 vs. 24‑hour average $89.4255, Ex. C), suggesting a short‑term corrective bounce is more probable than a continuation of the 6.61% weekly decline (Ex. C).  

3. Liquidity is robust (24‑hour volume $848.45 M, Ex. E) and the Chainlink feed, which governs settlement, is priced 0.97% higher than spot (Ex. F, G); this premium creates a clear arbitrage edge for a short practice position that can be entered at $89.9725 and settled at the lower spot without market impact.  

The Bear rests.

Your Honor, the Bear’s first contention collapses under the arithmetic of Exhibit B: the spot sits at 30 % of the 24‑hour range, yet the range is a narrow $1.35 band, offering negligible upside potential; a modest rise would still leave price well below the midpoint, not “pull” it upward.  

Second, the Bear’s reliance on a “neutral” RSI (Exhibit D) ignores the broader bearish context: seven‑day price is down 6.61 % (Exhibit C) and the Fear index reads 28 (Exhibit F), indicating prevailing pessimism that outweighs any fleeting neutral momentum.  

Nothing further.

Your Honor, the Bull’s claim of “limited upside” misreads the range data: the spot sits only 30 % above the low, leaving 70 % of the band to the high—a sizable upside window, not compression [Ex. B, A]. Moreover, the Bull’s reliance on a “neutral” RSI ignores the price‑momentum divergence: the 24‑hour average ($89.4255) sits above the 72‑hour average ($90.2577) by 0.92 %, signaling a short‑term rebound trend despite a modest RSI reading [Ex. C]. Finally, the Chainlink feed is 0.97 % higher than spot, offering a built‑in upside for a long practice entry, not a penalty [Ex. G]. Nothing further.

ruling.holding: The Court finds that the preponderance of evidence supports a short practice position for SOL/USD.

findings.finding: Spot price is $89.11, down 1.15% in 24h, indicating recent weakness
Seven‑day trend is –6.61% and 24‑h average is below the 72‑h average, showing continued down pressure
Fear & Greed Index at 28 (Fear) signals bearish sentiment
Chainlink feed is 0.97% above spot, creating a built‑in advantage for a short entered at the higher feed and settled at lower spot

ruling.opinion: The exhibits demonstrate that SOL is trading below recent averages, in a declining weekly trend, and amid fear‑driven sentiment. The price sits near the low end of a narrow range, limiting upside, while volatility is modest, reducing the chance of a sudden rally. The Chainlink reference price, higher than spot, gives a short trader a clear arbitrage edge at settlement. Collectively these factors justify a short practice position over the next 24 hours.
ruling.dissent: The Bull might argue that the RSI near 40 and the remaining 70% of the daily range allow a modest rebound, but the weight of trend, sentiment, and the settlement premium outweighs that view.
